p.src: Now Li Kui burst out of the inn, an axe in each hand, and was about to race to the city wall and hack through a gate when Yan Qing seized him around the waist and hips and, with a single throw, sent his feet flying skyward. Yan Qing hauled him up and immediately set off along a side road; Li Kui had no choice but to follow. Why was Li Kui afraid of Yan Qing? As it happened, Yan Qing was the finest wrestler under heaven, and for that reason Song Gongming had expressly ordered him to keep watch over Li Kui. Whenever Li Kui refused to obey him, Yan Qing's wrestling hands could bring him down with a single throw. Li Kui had often felt the force of his hands and feet; hence he feared him and could only submit. Yan Qing and Li Kui dared not take the highway, fearing that troops might pursue them and prove too much to resist, so they made a wide detour toward the road to Chenliu County. Li Kui put his clothes back on and hid the great axes beneath his robe. Having lost his headcloth, he parted his tawny hair and tied it into two side-buns. They travelled until daybreak. Yan Qing had money on him, so they bought wine and meat at a village inn, ate, and then lengthened their strides and hurried onward. At dawn the next day, the capital was in a great uproar. Grand Marshal Gao led troops out of the city, but, unable to catch the fugitives, returned. Li Shishi merely professed to know nothing. Grand Marshal Yang also returned home to recuperate. A tally of those injured in the city came to four or five hundred, while those hurt by being knocked down or trampled were beyond counting. Grand Marshal Gao joined Tong Guan of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and together they went to the Grand Tutor's residence to confer, proposing that troops be mobilized without delay to hunt down and destroy the outlaws.

p.src: Meanwhile, Li Kui and Yan Qing travelled on until they reached a place called Four Willows Village, where night overtook them. The two made for a large manor, knocked open the gate, and went straight into the thatched reception hall. The master of the manor, Old Squire Di, came out to receive them. Seeing Li Kui with his hair tied in two side-buns but no Daoist robe, and with an exceedingly ugly face besides, he could not imagine what sort of man he might be. The old squire casually asked Yan Qing, “Where does this reverend master come from?” Yan Qing laughed. “This master is an extraordinary fellow. None of you can fathom him. Just give us whatever supper you have and lodge us for the night; we shall leave early tomorrow.” Li Kui said nothing. On hearing this, the old squire fell to the floor and bowed before Li Kui, saying, “Master, please save your disciple!” Li Kui said, “What do you want me to save you from? Tell me the truth.” The old squire said, “My household numbers over a hundred souls. My wife and I have only one daughter of our own, now more than twenty years old. Six months ago an evil spirit possessed her, and since then she has remained in her room and never comes out even to ask for food or drink. If anyone goes to call her, she hurls bricks and stones wildly, and everyone in the household has been injured by her. Time after time we have invited exorcists here, but none has been able to catch it.” Li Kui said, “Old Squire, I am a disciple of the Perfected Master Luo of Jizhou. I can soar through the clouds and ride the mists, and catching ghosts is my particular skill. If you are willing to part with the necessary provisions, I shall catch the ghost for you tonight. First, I require a pig and a sheep as offerings to the divine generals.” The old squire said, “We have plenty of pigs and sheep, and wine goes without saying.” Li Kui said, “Choose the fattest, slaughter them, and boil them until tender. I shall also need several jars of fine wine. Have everything prepared. At the third watch tonight, I shall catch the ghost for you.” The old squire said, “Master, should you require paper and materials for writing talismans, I have those in the house as well.” Li Kui said, “My magic has only one method; I need none of those damned talismans. Once I enter the room, I shall drag the ghost straight out.” Yan Qing could no longer suppress his laughter. The old man took all this for earnest talk. He spent half the night making preparations; when both pig and sheep had been thoroughly cooked, they were set out in the hall. Li Kui called for ten large bowls and ten jars of piping-hot wine, which he had poured out in one round. Two candles burned brilliantly, and a brazier of fine incense blazed with leaping flames. Li Kui fetched a bench and seated himself in the middle, without reciting a single word. Drawing the great axe from his waist, he hacked open the pig and sheep, tore off great chunks, and ate them. Then he called to Yan Qing, “Brother Little Yi, come and eat some too.” Yan Qing gave a cold laugh and would not come over to eat. Li Kui ate his fill and drank five or six bowls of fine wine, leaving the old squire staring in astonishment. Li Kui then called to all the manor servants, “Come and share the blessed offerings.” In the twinkling of an eye, the remaining meat had all been distributed. Li Kui said, “Quickly bring a bucket of hot water so we can wash our hands and feet.” Before long, they had washed their hands and feet, and Li Kui asked the old squire for tea and drank it. Then he asked Yan Qing, “Have you eaten or not?” Yan Qing replied, “I have eaten my fill.” Li Kui said to the old squire, “The wine has made us drunk and the meat has filled our bellies. We have a journey ahead tomorrow, so we gentlemen are going to bed.” The old squire cried, “What a calamity! When, then, will the ghost be caught?” Li Kui said, “If you truly want me to catch the ghost, have someone lead me to your daughter's room.” The old squire said, “But that supernatural being is in the room at this very moment, hurling bricks and stones everywhere. Who would dare go near it?”

p.src: Li Kui drew both his broad axes and ordered the men to hold the torches at a distance to light his way. Striding boldly, Li Kui rushed straight to the room and saw a faint light within. When Li Kui peered inside, he saw a young man embracing a woman as they talked. Li Kui kicked the door open, and where his axe struck, sparks burst and crashes rang out like thunder. Looking closely, he discovered that he had overturned the lamp with his blow. The young man was about to flee, but Li Kui gave a great roar and, with one sweep of his axe, struck him down. The woman crawled beneath the bed and hid. Li Kui first chopped off the man's head with one blow, set it on the bed, then struck the bedstead with his axe and shouted, “Woman, come out at once! If you do not crawl out, I shall hack you and the bed alike to pieces!” The woman cried repeatedly, “Spare my life, and I will come out.” She had only just poked out her head when Li Kui seized her by the hair, dragged her beside the corpse, and demanded, “Who was that fellow I killed?” The woman replied, “He was my lover, Wang Xiao'er.” Li Kui asked again, “Where did the bricks and food come from?” The woman said, “I gave him my gold, silver, and jewelry, and during the second or third watch he carried them in over the wall.” Li Kui said, “What use is there in keeping such a filthy woman as you!” He dragged her to the bed and chopped off her head with one stroke. He tied the two heads together, then laid the woman's corpse beside the man's body. Li Kui said, “I have eaten my fill and had nowhere to work it off.” He stripped off his upper garments, took up both axes, and, facing the two corpses, hacked high and low in a wild flurry as though beating a challenge drum. Li Kui laughed and said, “Plainly these two will not come back to life.” He tucked away his great axes, lifted the heads, and strode out before the hall shouting, “I have caught both ghosts!” He flung down the heads, startling everyone in the manor. When they all came to look, they recognized one as the old master's daughter, but no one knew the other head. One of the farmhands studied it for a while and said, “It looks somewhat like Wang Xiao'er, the bird-limer from the eastern village.” Li Kui said, “This farmhand has sharp eyes!” The old master asked, “Master, how did you learn the truth?” Li Kui replied, “Your daughter was hiding under the bed. When I dragged her out and questioned her, she said, ‘He is my lover, Wang Xiao'er, and all the food I ate was brought in by him.’ Only after questioning her about every detail did I strike.” The old master wept and said, “Master, you might at least have spared my daughter.” Li Kui cursed him: “You damned old ox! Your daughter secretly took a lover, yet you still wanted her spared! If you carry on weeping like this, you will repay me with blame instead of thanks. I shall have words with you tomorrow.” Yan Qing found a room, and he and Li Kui went to rest. The old master led some men with lamps and candles into the room. There they saw the two headless bodies, hacked into more than ten pieces and scattered over the floor. The old man and his wife wept in grief, then ordered the servants to carry the remains behind the house and burn them. Li Kui slept until dawn, then sprang up and said to the old master, “I caught the ghosts for you last night. Why have you not thanked me?” The old master had no choice but to prepare wine and food for them. After Li Kui and Yan Qing had eaten, they departed. Old Master Di attended to his household affairs. But no more need be said of that.

p.src: Now Li Kui and Yan Qing left Four Willows Village and resumed their journey. The grass was withered, the land stretched wide, the trees had shed their leaves, and the mountains stood bare. Nothing of note occurred along the road. Together they made a wide circuit north of Liangshan Marsh. Still seventy or eighty li from the stronghold and unable to reach the mountain, they came near Jingmen Town. As evening fell, they hurried to a large manor and knocked at the gate. Yan Qing said, “Let us find an inn and lodge there.” Li Kui said, “Surely a wealthy household like this is far better than any inn!” Before he had finished speaking, a farmhand came out and said to them, “Our old master is sorely troubled just now! You two must go elsewhere to lodge.” Li Kui marched straight inside. Yan Qing could not hold him back, and he went all the way to the thatched hall. Li Kui shouted, “We are travelers asking only one night's lodging. What damned great matter is that? You say the old master is troubled! Why, I am just the man to talk to someone with troubles!” When the old master peered out from within and saw how fierce Li Kui looked, he secretly ordered his people to receive them. They were shown to a side room beside the outer hall and told to rest there. Some food was prepared for them, and after they had eaten, they were told to go inside and sleep. After some time, the meal was brought out. The two ate and then settled down to rest. That night Li Kui had not a drop of wine. He tossed and turned sleeplessly on the earthen bed, hearing the old man and his wife sobbing within. Li Kui grew so vexed that he could not close his eyes. At last dawn came. He sprang up, went before the hall, and demanded, “Who in your household has been crying all night and keeping your lordship awake?” Hearing him, the old master had no choice but to come out and answer, “I have a daughter, just eighteen years old, who was carried off by force. That is why we grieve.” Li Kui said, “More mischief again! Who carried off your daughter?” The old master said, “If I tell you his name, you will be so frightened that you foul yourself! He is Song Jiang, chief of Liangshan Marsh, with one hundred and eight heroes under him, not counting his rank-and-file soldiers.” Li Kui asked, “First tell me this: how many men came with him?” The old master replied, “Two days ago, he came with a young fellow, each riding a horse.” Li Kui called to Yan Qing, “Brother Xiao Yi, come and hear what this old man says. Our elder brother is a hypocrite after all, and no good man!” Yan Qing said, “Brother, do not act rashly. This certainly cannot be true!” Li Kui said, “Even in the Eastern Capital he went to Li Shishi's house. Do you think he would not do such a thing here?” Li Kui then said to the old master, “If there is food in your manor, bring us some to eat. I shall tell you the truth: I am Li Kui, the ‘Black Whirlwind’ of Liangshan Marsh, and this man is Yan Qing, the ‘Prodigal.’ Since Song Jiang carried off your daughter, I shall go demand her back and return her to you.” The old master bowed and thanked him. Li Kui and Yan Qing went straight to Liangshan Marsh and made their way into the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness. When Song Jiang saw Li Kui and Yan Qing return, he asked, “Brothers, where have you two come from? You wandered far out of your way and have only now arrived.” Li Kui made no answer. His strange eyes bulging, he drew a great axe and first chopped down the apricot-yellow banner, then tore the four characters “Carry Out the Way on Heaven's Behalf” to shreds. Everyone was stunned. Song Jiang shouted, “What mischief are you up to now, you black rogue?” Wielding both axes, Li Kui charged into the hall and made straight for Song Jiang. A poem says:

p.src: Yan Qing stepped forward and said, “Brother, hear my full account of what happened along the way. Outside the Eastern Capital, he leapt out of the inn with his two axes, intending to hack down the gate, but I threw him to the ground and dragged him up. I told him, ‘Our brother has already left. What are you making such a scene here all by yourself for?’ Only then did he believe me, and we dared not travel by the main road. He had also lost his headcloth, so he twisted his hair into two childish buns. When we reached Siliu Village and the manor of Old Master Di, he posed as an exorcist come to catch a ghost, then seized the old man’s daughter and her lover and chopped them both into mincemeat. After that we climbed the mountain west of the main road, but he insisted on making a wide detour. As we drew near Jingmen Town, evening fell, so we sought lodging at Old Master Liu’s manor. All night he heard the old man and his wife weeping. Unable to sleep, he could scarcely wait for dawn before getting up to question them. Old Master Liu said, ‘Two days ago, Song Jiang of Liangshan Marsh and a young fellow rode up to the manor on two horses. Hearing that they were men who carried out Heaven’s justice, I had my eighteen-year-old daughter come out to serve them wine. They drank until midnight, then the two of them carried my daughter off.’ When Brother Li Kui heard this, he took it for the truth. Again and again I explained, ‘Our brother is not that kind of man. There are many scoundrels abroad who shelter beneath another’s fame, borrow his name, and commit outrages.’ But Brother Li said, ‘When I saw him in the Eastern Capital, he was still infatuated with the singing girl Li Shishi and could not bear to leave her. If it was not him, who else could it be?’ That is why he flew into a rage.” When Song Jiang had heard him out, he said, “How can such a false accusation be proved? Why did you not tell me?” Li Kui said, “I have always regarded you as a true hero, but it turns out you are a beast! What a fine deed you have done!” Song Jiang shouted, “Just listen to me! I returned with two or three thousand troops. If two horsemen had broken away from the road, it could never have been hidden from everyone. And if I had abducted a woman, she would surely be here in the stronghold. Go search my quarters and see for yourself.” Li Kui said, “Brother, what damned nonsense are you talking? Everyone in the stronghold is under your command, and plenty of them protect you. Where could they not have hidden her? I once respected you as a hero untouched by lust, but you are a rake given to wine and women after all. Killing Yan Poxi was only a small example; keeping Li Shishi in the Eastern Capital was the great one. Do not deny it. Send the girl back to Old Liu at once, and there may still be room to settle this. If you will not return his daughter, then whether I act early or late, sooner or later I will kill you.” Song Jiang said, “Stop your uproar. Old Master Liu is still alive and all his servants are there; we shall go together and confront them. If they identify me, I will stretch out my neck there and take the blow of your axe. But if they do not, what punishment do you deserve for showing such insubordination?” Li Kui said, “If I fail to prove it against you, I will forfeit this head to you!” Song Jiang said, “Excellent. All you brothers shall be witnesses.” He had Pei Xuan, the Iron-Faced Recorder, draw up two written military pledges for the wager, and each man signed his own. Song Jiang’s pledge was entrusted to Li Kui, and Li Kui’s to Song Jiang. Li Kui added, “The young fellow was none other than Chai Jin.” Chai Jin said, “Then I shall go with you.” Li Kui said, “You had better come. If they identify you there, even if you are Lord Chai—or Lord Mi, for all I care—you will still taste a few strokes of my axe.” Chai Jin said, “That is no concern. You go on ahead and wait there. If we all go together, there may be some trickery.” Li Kui said, “Quite right.

u.src: Yan Qing stepped forward and said, “Brother, hear my full account of what happened along the way.
Outside the Eastern Capital, he leapt out of the inn with his two axes, intending to hack down the gate, but I threw him to the ground and dragged him up.
I told him, ‘Our brother has already left. What are you making such a scene here all by yourself for?’
Only then did he believe me, and we dared not travel by the main road.
He had also lost his headcloth, so he twisted his hair into two childish buns.
When we reached Siliu Village and the manor of Old Master Di, he posed as an exorcist come to catch a ghost, then seized the old man’s daughter and her lover and chopped them both into mincemeat.
After that we climbed the mountain west of the main road, but he insisted on making a wide detour.
As we drew near Jingmen Town, evening fell, so we sought lodging at Old Master Liu’s manor.
All night he heard the old man and his wife weeping. Unable to sleep, he could scarcely wait for dawn before getting up to question them.

Old Master Liu said, ‘Two days ago, Song Jiang of Liangshan Marsh and a young fellow rode up to the manor on two horses. Hearing that they were men who carried out Heaven’s justice, I had my eighteen-year-old daughter come out to serve them wine.
They drank until midnight, then the two of them carried my daughter off.’
When Brother Li Kui heard this, he took it for the truth.
Again and again I explained, ‘Our brother is not that kind of man. There are many scoundrels abroad who shelter beneath another’s fame, borrow his name, and commit outrages.’
But Brother Li said, ‘When I saw him in the Eastern Capital, he was still infatuated with the singing girl Li Shishi and could not bear to leave her. If it was not him, who else could it be?’
That is why he flew into a rage.”
When Song Jiang had heard him out, he said, “How can such a false accusation be proved?
Why did you not tell me?”
Li Kui said, “I have always regarded you as a true hero, but it turns out you are a beast!
What a fine deed you have done!”
Song Jiang shouted, “Just listen to me!
I returned with two or three thousand troops. If two horsemen had broken away from the road, it could never have been hidden from everyone.
And if I had abducted a woman, she would surely be here in the stronghold.
Go search my quarters and see for yourself.”
Li Kui said, “Brother, what damned nonsense are you talking?
Everyone in the stronghold is under your command, and plenty of them protect you. Where could they not have hidden her?
I once respected you as a hero untouched by lust, but you are a rake given to wine and women after all. Killing Yan Poxi was only a small example;
keeping Li Shishi in the Eastern Capital was the great one.
Do not deny it. Send the girl back to Old Liu at once, and there may still be room to settle this.
If you will not return his daughter, then whether I act early or late, sooner or later I will kill you.”
Song Jiang said, “Stop your uproar. Old Master Liu is still alive and all his servants are there; we shall go together and confront them.
If they identify me, I will stretch out my neck there and take the blow of your axe.
But if they do not, what punishment do you deserve for showing such insubordination?”
Li Kui said, “If I fail to prove it against you, I will forfeit this head to you!”
Song Jiang said, “Excellent. All you brothers shall be witnesses.”
He had Pei Xuan, the Iron-Faced Recorder, draw up two written military pledges for the wager, and each man signed his own.

p.src: Yan Qing and Li Kui returned to Old Master Liu’s manor. The old master received them and asked, “Good sir, how did the matter fare?” Li Kui said, “Song Jiang himself is coming now to have you identify him. You, your wife, and all the servants must look carefully. If it is indeed he, speak the truth without fear. I shall see justice done for you.” Just then a servant reported, “More than a dozen horsemen have arrived at the manor.” Li Kui said, “That will be them. The men and horses have halted off to one side, and only Song Jiang and Chai Jin are coming in.” Song Jiang and Chai Jin went straight to the thatched hall and sat down. Li Kui stood to one side clutching his broad axe. He waited only for the old man to say yes, whereupon he meant to strike. Old Master Liu came forward and bowed to Song Jiang. Li Kui asked the old man, “Is this the man who carried off your daughter?” The old man opened his dim, rheumy eyes wide, summoned what remained of his aged vigor, stared hard, and said, “No.” Song Jiang said to Li Kui, “What have you to say now?” Li Kui said, “You two glare at him first. The old man is afraid of you and so dares not say it was you.” Song Jiang said, “Call everyone in the manor here to identify me.” Li Kui immediately summoned all the servants to identify him, but they cried with one voice, “It was not he.” Song Jiang said, “Old Master Liu, I am Song Jiang of Liangshan Marsh, and this brother here is Chai Jin. Your daughter was carried off by impostors using false names. If you discover who they are, send word to the stronghold, and I shall see justice done for you.” Song Jiang then said to Li Kui, “I shall not argue with you here. Once you return to the stronghold, this matter will be judged.” Song Jiang and Chai Jin went back to the main stronghold first with their company of horsemen. Yan Qing asked, “Brother Li, what are we to do?” Li Kui said, “It was only my hasty temper that made me do wrong. Since I have forfeited this head, I will cut it off myself with one stroke, and you can take it back and present it to our brother.” Yan Qing said, “Why seek death for no reason? I will teach you a way called ‘bearing the thorn rods to ask forgiveness.’” Li Kui asked, “How does one bear the thorn rods?” Yan Qing said, “Take off your clothes, bind yourself with hempen rope, carry a bundle of thorn rods on your bare back, and prostrate yourself before the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness, saying, ‘Brother, beat me as much as you please.’ He will naturally be unable to bring himself to strike you. That is what is meant by ‘bearing the thorn rods to ask forgiveness.’” Li Kui said, “It sounds well enough, but it is rather humiliating. Better to cut off my head and be done with it.” Yan Qing said, “Everyone in the stronghold is your brother. Who would laugh at you?” Li Kui had no choice but to return to the stronghold with Yan Qing, bearing the thorn rods to ask forgiveness.

p.src: Meanwhile, Song Jiang and Chai Jin returned first to the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness. As they were discussing Li Kui’s affair with the other brothers, the Black Whirlwind appeared stark naked, carrying a bundle of thorn rods on his back. He knelt before the hall with his head bowed and said not a word. Song Jiang laughed. “You black brute, why have you come bearing thorn rods? Do you think this alone will make me pardon you?” Li Kui said, “Your brother was in the wrong! Brother, choose a stout cudgel and give me a few dozen blows!” Song Jiang said, “You and I wagered your head. Why have you come bearing thorn rods instead?” Li Kui replied, “If you will not forgive me, Brother, then bring a knife and cut off this head. That will settle it.” Everyone present pleaded on Li Kui’s behalf. Song Jiang said, “If you want me to pardon him, let him capture those two false Song Jiangs and recover Old Squire Liu’s daughter for him. Only then will I forgive you.” Hearing this, Li Kui sprang to his feet and cried, “I’ll catch them as easily as a turtle in a jar—they’ll fall straight into my hands!” Song Jiang said, “They are two formidable men and have two saddled horses besides. How can you approach them all by yourself? Have Yan Qing go with you.” Yan Qing said, “At your command, Brother. I am willing to go.” He went to his room, fetched his crossbow, took up an eyebrow-high staff, and followed Li Kui back to Old Squire Liu’s manor. Yan Qing questioned him closely about what had happened. Old Squire Liu said, “They arrived when the sun was sinking westward and left during the third watch. I do not know where they went, and I dared not follow them. The leader was short, with a dark, lean face; the second was sturdily built, with a short beard and large eyes.” After learning all the details, the two said, “Set your mind at ease, Squire. Whatever happens, we shall rescue your daughter and return her to you! Our brother Song Gongming has commanded us to find and bring her back, and we dare not fail or delay.” They had dried meat boiled and steamed cakes prepared, packed them into their provision bags, fastened the bags at their sides, and departed from Old Squire Liu’s manor. They first searched due north, but found only desolate country devoid of habitation. After traveling for a day or two, they had discovered not the slightest trace. They then turned due east and searched for another two days, reaching the border between Lingzhou and Gaotang, but still found no news. Li Kui grew anxious and flushed with impatience. They doubled back and searched westward for two more days, yet heard not the slightest thing.

p.src: That night, the two lodged on the altar platform of an old temple beside a mountain. Li Kui could not sleep and rose to sit up. He suddenly heard footsteps outside the temple. Li Kui sprang up and opened the door to look. A man carrying a broad-bladed sword was rounding the temple and heading up the foot of the mountain behind it. Li Kui followed behind him. Hearing him, Yan Qing seized his crossbow and staff and followed. He called, “Brother Li, do not chase him. I have a plan.” The moonlight was dim that night. Yan Qing handed his staff to Li Kui, while in the distance they watched the man walk steadily on with his head lowered. Yan Qing drew near, set a bolt in place, and steadily released the crossbow string, saying, “Lucky bolt, do not fail me.” With that single shot, he struck the man squarely in the right leg, sending him sprawling to the ground. Li Kui rushed up, seized him by the collar, and dragged him straight back to the old temple. He roared, “Where have you taken Old Squire Liu’s daughter?” The man pleaded, “Good sirs, I know nothing of this affair. I have never abducted any daughter of Old Squire Liu. I merely waylay travelers here and do a little petty business. How would I dare commit anything so grave as stealing another family’s daughter?” Li Kui bound the man into a bundle, raised his axe, and shouted, “If you do not tell the truth, I’ll chop you into twenty pieces!” The man cried, “Please release me first, and we can discuss it!” Yan Qing said, “My man, let me first pull out this bolt for you.” After releasing him, he asked, “Who was it, then, that truly abducted Old Squire Liu’s daughter? Since you waylay travelers around here, surely you must have heard some rumor of it?” The man said, “I can only make a guess and do not know the truth. About fifteen li northwest of here stands a mountain called Ox-Head Mountain. There was formerly a Daoist monastery upon it. Recently it was seized by two brigands, one surnamed Wang and named Jiang, the other surnamed Dong and named Hai. Both are common outlaws of the greenwood. They first killed all the Daoist priests and novices, then occupied the monastery with only five or seven followers and made a practice of descending the mountain to plunder. Wherever they go, they call themselves Song Jiang. Most likely those two were the ones who abducted her.” Yan Qing said, “There seems to be something behind your story. Do not fear us, my man! I am Yan Qing, the Prodigal of Liangshan Marsh, and this is Li Kui, the Black Whirlwind. I will tend your arrow wound, and you shall guide the two of us there.” The man replied, “I am willing to go.” Yan Qing found the man’s broad-bladed sword and returned it to him, then bound up his wound. Taking advantage of the faint moonlight, Yan Qing and Li Kui supported him along the fifteen-li road. When they reached the mountain, they saw that it was not very high and truly resembled an ox’s head. The three climbed the mountain before dawn had broken. At the summit, they found the place completely encircled by an earthen wall, with some twenty rooms inside. Li Kui said, “Let us jump over the wall first.” Yan Qing said, “Wait until daybreak before we deal with them.” But Li Kui could not restrain himself and sprang over in a bound. A shout arose within. As the gate opened, a man came charging out at Li Kui with his broad-bladed sword leveled. Yan Qing, fearing the affair might be ruined, planted his staff and vaulted over the wall as well. The wounded guide fled like a puff of smoke. Yan Qing saw the man who had emerged locked in combat with Li Kui. Stealing forward unseen, he struck him squarely on the cheekbone with his staff. The man toppled into Li Kui’s arms, and Li Kui brought him down with a single axe-blow to the back. Not another person emerged from within. Yan Qing said, “Those scoundrels must have escaped by a rear passage.

p.src: Her tiny bound feet rose beneath spring gauze; fragrance steeped the jade-soft hollow of her breast. Such delicate beauty could scarcely endure the sudden storm; overwhelmed by hidden grief, she knitted her autumn-wave brows.

p.src: Yan Qing asked, “Are you not the daughter of Squire Liu?” The woman replied, “More than ten days ago, these two brigands abducted me and brought me here. Each night, they took turns forcing me to sleep with them. Day and night my tears fell like rain, and I sought a way to die, but they watched me too closely. Today, General, you have rescued me. You are as parents who have given me life anew.” Yan Qing said, “They had two horses. Where are they kept?” The woman said, “In the room on the eastern side.” Yan Qing saddled them and led them outside, then gathered up the gold and silver hoarded in the room, amounting to some three to five thousand taels. Yan Qing had the woman mount one horse, wrapped up the gold and silver, picked up the severed heads, and tied them all upon the other horse. Li Kui bound together a bundle of straw and, using the dying lamp beneath the window, set fire to the thatched hut on all four sides. The two opened the gate in the wall and escorted the woman down the mountain on foot, all the way to Squire Liu’s manor. When her parents saw their daughter, they were overjoyed, and all their sorrow vanished. They came forward together to bow and thank the two chieftains. Yan Qing said, “Do not thank the two of us. Come to the stronghold and offer your thanks to our elder brother Song Gongming.” Neither man would partake of food or wine. Each mounted a horse, and they galloped back up the mountain. By the time they returned to the stronghold and reached the Third Pass, the red sun was touching the mountains. Leading the horses laden with gold and silver and carrying the heads, the two went straight to the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness to pay their respects to Song Jiang. Yan Qing related the entire affair in detail. Song Jiang was delighted. He ordered the heads buried, the gold and silver placed in the treasury, and the horses turned into the herd of warhorses to be tended. The following day, a banquet was laid to celebrate Yan Qing and Li Kui’s success. Squire Liu also gathered up gold and silver and came up the mountain to the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness to thank Song Jiang. Song Jiang would by no means accept it. He gave the squire food and wine, then had him escorted down the mountain and back to his manor. Of this there is no more to tell. There was nothing further to report at Liangshan Marsh, and time passed swiftly before anyone knew it.

p.src: Willows gradually donned their gosling-yellow, and ripples slowly took on a mallard green. Peach cheeks clustered thick with crimson blossoms, while apricot faces gently opened their scarlet buds. Flowers before the hills and trees behind them all put forth new shoots; duckweed by the banks and reeds in the water all returned to life. The first clear day after Grain Rain was truly weather fit for fair ladies; the Cold Food fire ban had only just passed, and the splendor of the third month was at its height.

p.src: As Song Jiang sat in the hall, a band of men was brought up from the pass. The guards reported, “We have seized a party of cattle dealers. They have seven or eight carts and several bundles of quarterstaffs.” When Song Jiang looked them over, he saw that they were all burly, imposing men. Kneeling before the hall, they pleaded, “We humble men have come directly from Fengxiang Prefecture and are now on our way to Tai’an Prefecture to burn incense. The twenty-eighth day of the third month is the birthday of the Holy Emperor of the Eastern Peak. We are all going to perform with our staffs upon the platform. The contests last three days running, and there are no fewer than a thousand bouts there. This year there is a formidable wrestler from Taiyuan Prefecture, surnamed Ren and named Yuan. He stands ten feet tall and calls himself ‘Pillar That Props Up Heaven.’ He boasts, ‘In wrestling, none beneath heaven can match me; in contests throughout the realm, I alone rank first.’ We hear that for the past two years he has competed at the temple without meeting a worthy opponent and has carried off all manner of prizes with ease. This year he has posted another challenge, inviting all men under heaven to wrestle him. We humble men came because of him: first, to burn incense; second, to see what Ren Yuan can do; and third, to steal a lesson in some of his finest staff techniques. We beg Your Majesty to show us mercy.” On hearing this, Song Jiang ordered the guards, “Escort these men down the mountain at once. Not the smallest thing of theirs is to be violated. From now on, whenever you encounter pilgrims passing this way to burn incense, do not frighten them. Let them come and go freely.” Their lives thus spared, the men bowed their thanks and went down the mountain. Then Yan Qing rose and made a report to Song Jiang, speaking at great length—more than could be told in a single sitting. As a result, Tai’an Prefecture would be thrown into alarm, and Xiangfu County plunged into uproar. Indeed: within the Temple of the Eastern Peak, two tigers would battle; before the Jianing Hall, two dragons would contend. What, after all, did Yan Qing say? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
